Tidy Data" subtitle: Day 08 title-slide-attributes: data-background-image: ../img/horst_tidydata_4.jpg data-background-size: 70% data-background-position: bottom right data-background-opacity: "0.8" data-slide-number: none format: revealjs: incremental: true code-copy: true auto-stretch: false editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- ## The College Scorecard > The College Scorecard is designed to increase transparency, putting the power in the hands of the public — from those choosing colleges to those improving college quality — to see how well different schools are serving their students. ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 187 Columns: 13 $ unitid 228343, 177719, 367884, 149781, 135364, 212601, 133979,~ $ school "Southwestern University", "Barnes-Jewish College Goldf~ $ type "private", "private", "private", "private", "private", ~ $ city "Georgetown", "Saint Louis", "Fort Myers", "Wheaton", "~ $ state "TX", "MO", "FL", "IL", "GA", "PA", "FL", "CA", "IN", "~ $ region "Southwest", "Plains", "Southeast", "Great Lakes", "Sou~ $ admission_rate 0.4903, NA, 0.6121, 0.8481, 0.5000, 0.7552, 0.3999, 0.5~ $ act 26, NA, NA, 29, NA, 23, NA, 22, 25, 31, NA, NA, 20, 20,~ $ undergrads 1507, 569, 832, 2358, 235, 2866, 1049, 4516, 2120, 1545~ $ cost 55886, NA, 27425, 49214, NA, 44896, 27460, 58014, 46440~ $ grad_rate 0.6945, NA, 0.2621, 0.8878, 0.5000, 0.6770, 0.3644, 0.7~ $ fy_retention 0.8571, NA, 0.4783, 0.9262, NA, 0.8217, 0.6355, 0.8179,~ $ fedloan 0.5105, 0.8185, 0.6213, 0.4902, 0.5529, 0.5524, 0.6755,~ ``` ::: ::: ## Using `%>%` or `|>` We begin by building up a series of pipes: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="1|2|3"} mn_colleges <- colleges |> # dataframe first and then... filter(state == "MN") |> # filter out MN colleges and then... select(school, city, admission_rate:fedloan) # select the columns of interest ``` ::: ## The `|>` (base) pipe - `|>` pipe operator was introduced in R v4.1 - For simple uses, acts the same as `%>%` but is more rigid - I'll use both in class examples, but you can use `|>` or `%>%` # Calculating Summaries {.maize} ## Computing statistics: `summarize` - collapse many values down into a statistic - `summarize(data, newstat = fun(var))`
applies the `fun` function to `var` variable(s) and returns one value in `newstat` column ## Computing statistics: `summarize` ::: panel-tabset ### `dplyr` Average and SD of cost in a data frame format: ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} colleges %>% summarize( avg_cost = mean(cost, na.rm = TRUE), sd_cost = sd(cost , na.rm = TRUE) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 x 2 avg_cost sd_cost 1 36620. 16244. ``` ::: ::: ### `base` R ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mean(colleges$cost, na.rm = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 36619.72 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} sd(colleges$cost, na.rm = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 16243.9 ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Your turn ::: {.task .nonincremental} Using the `flights` data from the {nycflights23} package, use `summarize()` to compute statistics about the data: 1. The lowest and highest `distance` traveled 2. The lowest and highest `air_time` 3. The median `dep_delay` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: ## `group_by()` Groups cases by common values of one or more columns ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} colleges %>% group_by(state) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 187 x 13 # Groups: state [44] unitid school type city state region admission_rate act undergrads cost 1 228343 Southwe~ priv~ Geor~ TX South~ 0.490 26 1507 55886 2 177719 Barnes-~ priv~ Sain~ MO Plains NA NA 569 NA 3 367884 Hodges ~ priv~ Fort~ FL South~ 0.612 NA 832 27425 # i 184 more rows # i 3 more variables: grad_rate , fy_retention , fedloan ``` ::: ::: How does this help us? ## Spit-apply-combine ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](../img/08-split-apply-combine.png){width=1109} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ## Statistics by group: `group_by` + `summarize` Summary statistics **by state** ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} colleges %>% group_by(state) %>% summarize( n_schools = n(), avg_cost = mean(cost, na.rm = TRUE), min_size = min(undergrads, na.rm = TRUE), max_size = max(undergrads, na.rm = TRUE) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 44 x 5 state n_schools avg_cost min_size max_size 1 AL 4 22242. 245 7785 2 AR 3 43816. 512 1447 3 AZ 2 33388. 803 33715 4 CA 9 42807. 43 23337 5 CO 2 45574 5755 8448 6 CT 3 29895. 174 4425 7 FL 5 34747. 39 2401 8 GA 6 27961 235 9742 9 HI 1 36765 1558 1558 10 IA 1 NaN 339 339 # i 34 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Your turn ::: task Use `group_by()`, `summarize()`, and `slice_max()` to display the five `dest` airports with the most flights from NYC airports in 2023. Your display should include the median flight delay for these airports along with the number of flights to each airport. ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Calculating counts `count()` can be used as a short cut to `group_by() + summarize()` if you are only calculating counts ::: panel-tabset ### `group_by()` ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} colleges %>% group_by(state) %>% summarize(n = n()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 44 x 2 state n 1 AL 4 2 AR 3 3 AZ 2 4 CA 9 5 CO 2 6 CT 3 7 FL 5 8 GA 6 9 HI 1 10 IA 1 # i 34 more rows ``` ::: ::: ### `count()` ::: {.cell output-location='column'} ```{.r .cell-code} colleges %>% count(state) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 44 x 2 state n 1 AL 4 2 AR 3 3 AZ 2 4 CA 9 5 CO 2 6 CT 3 7 FL 5 8 GA 6 9 HI 1 10 IA 1 # i 34 more rows ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Calculations by group: `group_by` + `mutate` Calculate z-scores **within regions** ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code} colleges %>% group_by(region) %>% mutate(z_cost = (cost - mean(cost, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(cost, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% relocate(unitid:region, z_cost, everything()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 187 x 14 # Groups: region [10] unitid school type city state region z_cost admission_rate act undergrads 1 228343 South~ priv~ Geor~ TX South~ 1.51 0.490 26 1507 2 177719 Barne~ priv~ Sain~ MO Plains NA NA NA 569 3 367884 Hodge~ priv~ Fort~ FL South~ -0.467 0.612 NA 832 4 149781 Wheat~ priv~ Whea~ IL Great~ 1.06 0.848 29 2358 5 135364 Luthe~ priv~ Lith~ GA South~ NA 0.5 NA 235 6 212601 Ganno~ priv~ Erie PA Mid E~ 0.261 0.755 23 2866 7 133979 Flori~ priv~ Miam~ FL South~ -0.465 0.400 NA 1049 8 117140 Unive~ priv~ La V~ CA Far W~ 1.14 0.548 22 4516 9 152567 Trine~ priv~ Ango~ IN Great~ 0.849 0.816 25 2120 10 237057 Whitm~ priv~ Wall~ WA Far W~ 1.79 0.559 31 1545 # i 177 more rows # i 4 more variables: cost , grad_rate , fy_retention , # fedloan ``` ::: ::: ## `ungroup()` {.smaller} - Once data are grouped, they remain grouped until you manually ungroup them - Some summary functions ungroup them for you, e.g., `count()` and `summarize()` . . . ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} colleges %>% group_by(region) %>% mutate(z_cost = (cost - mean(cost, na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(cost, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% ungroup() %>% summarize(mean_z = mean(z_cost, na.rm = TRUE)) ``` ::: ::: panel-tabset ### With `ungroup()` ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 x 1 mean_z 1 -2.58e-18 ``` ::: ::: ### Without `ungroup()` ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 10 x 2 region mean_z 1 Far West -5.22e-17 2 Great Lakes 1.69e-16 3 Mid East 1.42e-16 4 New England -8.88e-17 5 Outlying Areas -2.22e-16 6 Plains -6.83e-17 7 Rocky Mountains 0 8 Southeast 2.02e-17 9 Southwest 6.94e-17 10 US Service Schools NaN ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Aside: code commenting In R, you can use `#` for adding comments to your code. Any text that follows the `#` will be printed as-is and won't be run as code. This is useful for leaving comments in your code and for temporarily disabling certain lines of code for debugging. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} colleges %>% group_by(state) %>% summarize( n_schools = n(), # This is a reminder to me # avg_cost = mean(cost, na.rm = TRUE), # This line isn't run min_size = min(undergrads, na.rm = TRUE), max_size = max(undergrads, na.rm = TRUE) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 44 x 4 state n_schools min_size max_size 1 AL 4 245 7785 2 AR 3 512 1447 3 AZ 2 803 33715 4 CA 9 43 23337 5 CO 2 5755 8448 6 CT 3 174 4425 7 FL 5 39 2401 8 GA 6 235 9742 9 HI 1 1558 1558 10 IA 1 339 339 # i 34 more rows ``` ::: ::: ## Aside: code commenting And it works especially well when you've used *chaining* in your code ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} colleges %>% #group_by(state) %>% summarize( n_schools = n(), avg_cost = mean(cost, na.rm = TRUE), min_size = min(undergrads, na.rm = TRUE), max_size = max(undergrads, na.rm = TRUE) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 x 4 n_schools avg_cost min_size max_size 1 187 36620. 0 33715 ``` ::: ::: # Intro to tidy data {.maize} ## ![](../img/horst_tidy_1.jpg) ## ![](../img/horst_tidy_2.jpg) ## ![](../img/horst_tidy_3.jpg) ## Bakeoff ratings - Ratings data for each episode in series 1-8 (in millions of viewers) . . . ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 8 x 11 series e1 e2 e3 e4 e5 e6 e7 e8 e9 e10 1 1 2.24 3 3 2.6 3.03 2.75 NA NA NA NA 2 2 3.1 3.53 3.82 3.6 3.83 4.25 4.42 5.06 NA NA 3 3 3.85 4.6 4.53 4.71 4.61 4.82 5.1 5.35 5.7 6.74 4 4 6.6 6.65 7.17 6.82 6.95 7.32 7.76 7.41 7.41 9.45 5 5 8.51 8.79 9.28 10.2 9.95 10.1 10.3 9.02 10.7 13.5 6 6 11.6 11.6 12.0 12.4 12.4 12 12.4 11.1 12.6 15.0 7 7 13.6 13.4 13.0 13.3 13.1 13.1 13.4 13.3 13.4 15.9 8 8 9.46 9.23 8.68 8.55 8.61 8.61 9.01 8.95 9.03 10.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: aside Source: [bakeoff](https://bakeoff.netlify.app/) R package ::: ## Discuss ::: {.task .nonincremental} Is this dataset in tidy format? <script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
